back: Information and communication technology: computers, software, networks, telecommunications and the internet used to collect, store, process, send and receive information.
Hardware is the physical equipment of a computer system; software is the programs that tell it what to do.
Hardware, software, networks, the internet and mobile technology.
Finance: accounting packages and online payment. Marketing: databases and websites. HR: records and payroll. Operations: stock control and design. Communication: email and messaging.
Speed, accuracy, lower cost of routine work, better information, wider markets and instant communication.
Cost, skills and training, security risks, dependence on power and networks, and job effects.
Passwords and access levels, backups kept away from the computer, antivirus and firewalls, encryption, control of who sees records and staff training.
Fear of job loss, lack of skills, discomfort with change and doubts about the benefits.
